feature: Feature 7 — Live Feed: the coins lane, and Trending
summary: The coins lane is a four-band ranked terminal board that answers "what is moving right now, and where did it come from" — the second half being the thing no competitor renders. Every row carries a STORY column occupying the slot DexScreener and Pump.fun spend on a sparkline, and it resolves to one of five states (confirmed / unverified / adopted / matching / none) so provenance is always visible, never implied. Trending is a separate, slower digest surface with an age FLOOR where the Live Feed has an age CEILING; that single boundary is why they are two surfaces and not one.
priorArt: PUMP.FUN BOARD — three lanes, not one list: 'Newly Created' (curve just opened), 'About to Graduate' (curve progress past ~50-75%), 'Graduated' (migrated off the curve to PumpSwap/Raydium). Per card: square thumbnail, NAME (TICKER), creator handle, market cap in USD, reply count, time-since-creation, and a bonding-curve progress bar as a percentage. Sorts: creation time, last trade, market cap, reply count. Cards flash on trade — motion is the liveness signal. Newer 'Advanced' view adds dev holding %, sniper count, bundled-buy %, top-10 holder %, and a 'dev sold' flag. RISK SIGNALLING IS ENTIRELY WALLET-BEHAVIOURAL — pump.fun does not show mint/freeze authority, because its own program revokes both at creation and the check would be a constant.

DEXSCREENER TRENDING — a true dense table. Columns: # / TOKEN (pair symbol, chain icon, DEX icon, paid 'boost' rocket) / PRICE / AGE / TXNS / VOLUME / MAKERS / 5M / 1H / 6H / 24H / LIQUIDITY / MCAP. A global time-window selector (5m / 1h / 6h / 24h) re-scopes TXNS, VOLUME, MAKERS and moves which change column is the sort key. The trending score is unpublished AND partially purchasable — 'Boosts' are a paid product, so rank position is not purely organic. Its 'Audit' panel shows: mint authority disabled, freeze authority disabled, LP burned %, top-10 holders %. For pump.fun tokens the first three are constants.

PHOTON / AXIOM — the professional layer. Adds per-row: dev holding %, snipers %, insiders %, bundlers %, top-10 %, holder count, and a composite 'audit' pill. Two UI mechanics worth stealing outright: freeze-on-hover (reordering queues while the pointer is over the list and applies on mouse-out) and never-reflow-below-the-fold (new entrants batch into a '3 new' pill instead of shoving rows).

WHAT INSIDOR KEEPS — the band split (pump.fun's three lanes are correct and become four); the dense right-aligned mono numeric table (DexScreener); curve progress as a first-class column; the 5m/1h/24h change triplet on graduated tokens; freeze-on-hover and the batched-new-entrant pill (Photon); wallet-behavioural risk over authority checks (pump.fun).

WHAT INSIDOR DROPS — (1) The 24h sparkline. It is 100px of the existing `.tk` grid rendering deterministic fake data (`ca.charCodeAt(1) + ageM%13`), and a 24h shape is undefined for the modal row on this board, which is minutes old. The STORY column takes its slot. (2) Mint-authority and freeze-authority as pass/fail rows — two permanent green ticks that train the user to ignore the panel. (3) Any paid rank placement; there is no boost product. (4) A single unified list across four orders of magnitude of market cap. (5) MCAP as a ranking term anywhere.

WHAT INSIDOR ADDS — (1) THE STORY COLUMN, with five states, carrying a lead-time chip (`+18m`) that is the product thesis rendered as a number: the story was display-eligible 18 minutes before this coin existed. (2) A 'From a Story' band that no other terminal can construct. (3) Band-specific column sets, so the Fresh band never renders three change columns that are structurally empty. (4) An exception-only safety model: signals that discriminate get a row; universal constants get dim context text and never a tick. (5) An explicit unknown count on the risk chip — the row states how many safety signals it could not obtain, so a clean chip cannot be manufactured by absence.
mechanism:
=== A. THE RANKING FORMULA ===

FOUR BANDS. Never one list. A 3-minute $8k curve and a $40M AMM token are not comparable
quantities and no single score across four orders of magnitude of mcap is meaningful.

  Fresh        curve_pct < 50 AND age <= 6h          -> CoinHeat_fresh
  Graduating   curve_pct >= 50 AND NOT migrated      -> curve_pct DESC, tiebreak coreHeat
  Live         migrated OR has an AMM pool           -> CoinHeat_live
  From a Story match_state='CONFIRMED'               -> CoinHeat_story   <- Insidor-only

Graduating sorts by PROGRESS, not heat. Progress is the entire reason a user opens that band.
Graduation threshold is SOL-denominated (~85 SOL in the curve). Read it from the program;
do NOT hardcode a USD figure, it moves with SOL.

SHARED INPUTS (5-minute window, from coin_snapshots -- does not exist yet, see dataContract):

  V5       = vol_buy_5m + vol_sell_5m                       USD
  V1h      = vol_buy_1h + vol_sell_1h                       USD
  traders5 = distinct makers in the 5m window
  netBuy   = (buyers_5m - sellers_5m) / max(traders5, 1)     in [-1, 1]
  accel    = (V5 * 12) / max(V1h, 1)                         1.0 = steady state
  breadth  = clamp(log1p(traders5) / log1p(50), 0, 1)
  org      = (organic_buy_5m + organic_sell_5m) / max(V5,1)  Jupiter, ONLY when age >= 10min

  quality      = (0.30 + 0.70*org) * clamp(1 + 0.5*netBuy, 0.6, 1.5) * safetyMult   age >= 10m
  quality_cold =                     clamp(1 + 0.5*netBuy, 0.6, 1.5) * safetyMult   age <  10m

  coreHeat = log1p(V5) * breadth * min(accel, 6)^0.5 * quality

  CoinHeat_fresh = coreHeat / ((age_min + 20)/20)^0.9
  CoinHeat_live  = coreHeat                                   no age term
  CoinHeat_story = coreHeat * (0.5 + 0.5 * narrative_heat_norm)

THE COLD-START PATH IS MANDATORY, NOT AN EDGE CASE. Jupiter states outright that fresh
tokens have volatile organic scores "because there isn't enough history," and every
SwapStats field is nullable. Under 10 minutes -- precisely Insidor's window -- the formula
must not read organicScore at all. That is what quality_cold is for.

WHY log1p(V5) AND NOT A POWER: coin volume spans six orders of magnitude on one board.
WHY min(accel, 6): an uncapped acceleration term is the single easiest thing in this design
to wash-trade -- one 5-minute burst would buy rank one.

=== WHAT PREVENTS A $1.8B TOKEN OWNING RANK ONE ===
Four mechanisms, in order of load-bearing-ness:

1. BAND PARTITION. A $1.8B token is in the Live band. It structurally cannot appear above a
   curve token, because they are never in the same ordered list. This is not a tuning
   parameter that can drift -- it is the table structure.

2. MCAP AND LIQUIDITY ARE NOT TERMS. CoinHeat reads 5-minute volume, trader breadth,
   net-buyer ratio and acceleration. It never reads market cap. Mcap is a display column and
   a gate. A $1.8B token with flat 5-minute flow scores near zero, correctly.

3. ACCELERATION IS SELF-NORMALISED. accel = V5*12 / V1h compares the token to ITS OWN last
   hour. A big token must be beating itself to rank; it gets no credit for being big. This is
   the term doing the actual work.

4. THE AGE PENALTY IN THE FRESH BAND. ((age+20)/20)^0.9 -> 1.87x at 20m, 3.48x at 60m,
   7.94x at 3h. A 3-hour coin needs 4.2x the coreHeat of a 20-minute coin to hold position.
   The Fresh band turns over completely in roughly 40 minutes.

PRESENTED HEAT: round(100 * min(1, CoinHeat / p95_CoinHeat_1h_within_band)). Per band, so
each band self-calibrates -- a dead night still shows spread, a wild night is not all 100s.

DOES A STORY LINK BOOST RANK IN THE OTHER THREE BANDS? NO -- deliberately. If story
attachment multiplied rank in Fresh/Graduating/Live, the incentive would be to game the
matcher, and the matcher is the 0.97-precision-critical component. Story presence is a
FILTER (its own band) and a TIEBREAK ONLY (applied after CoinHeat, before liquidity).
Keeping it out of the multiplier keeps the attack surface off the correctness-critical path.

=== B. HARD GATES (row hidden unless "Show risky" is on -- a loud toggle, not a drawer checkbox) ===

  mint_authority_active
  freeze_authority_active
  band='live' AND liquidity < $3,000
  sells_5m = 0 AND buys_5m > 30                        honeypot proxy
  mint_time IS NULL                                    FAIL CLOSED
  top10_pct > 60   (Live/Graduating)  |  > 85 (Fresh)  BAND-DEPENDENT -- see below

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE GATE LIST IN 03-system-design §4.4, both of which would otherwise
empty the Fresh band on day one:

 (a) A flat top10_pct > 60 gate applied to Fresh deletes the band. A 3-minute-old curve
     token legitimately has concentrated holders -- there have only been nine buyers. The
     threshold must be band-dependent: 85% on Fresh, 60% on Live.
 (b) On a pump.fun curve the LARGEST TOKEN ACCOUNT IS THE BONDING CURVE PDA ITSELF, holding
     the unsold supply. If it is included in the concentration calculation, every single
     pre-graduation token reads as 80-95% concentrated and the signal is destroyed. The
     curve PDA must be excluded from top-N holder math and from holder_count. This is the
     difference between a working risk column and a column of red.

 mint_time IS NULL failing closed is a live defect: lib/token-lookup.js:70 currently reads
 `if (!pair.pairCreatedAt) return 0;` -- missing timestamp renders as ageMin = 0, i.e.
 "brand new," which is maximally attractive on a terminal that sells earliness. Delete it.

=== C. SAFETY MULTIPLIER (soft; the gates above are separate) ===

  safetyMult = 1.0
    * (top10_pct > 60 ? 0.35 : top10_pct > 40 ? 0.70 : 1.0)     curve PDA excluded
    * (top1_pct  > 25 ? 0.50 : 1.0)
    * (holder_count < 25 ? 0.60 : 1.0)
    * (sells_5m = 0 AND buys_5m > 30 ? 0.20 : 1.0)
    * (creator_prior_rugs >= 2 ? 0.30
       : creator_prior_mints >= 20 AND creator_median_peak_mcap < 15000 ? 0.55 : 1.0)
    * (band='live' AND liquidity < 3000 ? 0.40 : 1.0)
    clamped to [0.15, 1.0]

  Plus two cheap local wash detectors from §4.5: trade-size Gini < 0.25 over >= 30 trades
  -> x0.5; more than 60% of trades at exactly 0.1 / 0.5 / 1.0 SOL -> x0.6.

  dev_holding_pct, sniper_pct and bundle_pct are ABSENT from this product. They require
  first-slot transaction analysis we are not building at MVP. They must NOT silently
  multiply by 1.0 -- they increment `unknown_signal_count`, which the row renders.

=== D. CREATOR HISTORY FOR FREE ===
The one behavioural signal we CAN build without an indexer. §3 already runs a PumpPortal
websocket over every Solana mint as the prospective earliness clock (t_mint). That stream
carries the creator wallet on every create event. Persisting it gives, after ~14 days of
accumulation and at zero marginal cost:
  creator_prior_mints, creator_median_peak_mcap, creator_rug_count
  (rug := peak_mcap >= $30k AND current_mcap <= 0.1 * peak_mcap AND age >= 24h)
This is the only row-level signal that discriminates as well as dev% and it is already
flowing through infrastructure built for a different purpose.

=== E. TRENDING'S FORMULA IS DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT ===
The Live Feed asks "what is moving in the last five minutes." Trending asks "what should I
know about." Keep the shipped trendScore weights -- they are settled -- and add a safety
multiplier and an eligibility floor:

  trendScore = 0.40*min(vol24h/mcap / 3, 1)
             + 0.25*min(txns24h / 4800, 1)
             + 0.20*min(max(chg24h,0) / 85, 1)
             + 0.15*min(max(chg1h,0) / 55, 1)
             ) * safetyMult
  Eligibility: mcap >= $30k AND liquidity >= $5k AND age >= 30min AND vol24h >= $10k
  Tiebreak: has CONFIRMED story, then vol24h.
  Recompute: 5 min (vs 20 s rank commit on the Live Feed).

THE LIVE FEED FRESH BAND HAS AN AGE CEILING OF 6h. TRENDING HAS AN AGE FLOOR OF 30m. That
one sentence is the entire justification for two surfaces; without it Trending is just a
slower copy of the board.

=== F. RANK STABILITY (both surfaces, from §4.3) ===
  EPS_SWAP = 0.08   ENTER_TICKS = 2   EXIT_TICKS = 3   PIN_MS = 90_000   MAX_MOVE = 5
  Freeze-on-hover: queue reorders while the pointer is inside the table, apply on mouse-out.
  Never reflow below the fold: new entrants above row 12 batch into a "3 new" pill.
  Values update live every tick unconditionally from a Map<mint, Row>; only the ORDERING
  array is held. Escape hatch: a coin whose V5 exceeds a hard threshold skips the 2-tick
  dwell and enters immediately with a NEW badge -- the dwell otherwise costs 40 seconds of
  the product's core claim.
dataContract:
THE HEADLINE: THE COIN LANE HAS NO TABLE. `narrative_tickers` is the only coin storage in
the schema and it is NARRATIVE-SCOPED, with narrative_id as its spine. A coin with no story
-- which is 85-95% of every row on this board -- has nowhere to live. This is not a missing
column, it is a missing entity. Everything below follows from that.

--- EXISTS TODAY ---
narrative_tickers: id, narrative_id, ticker, name, mcap, liquidity, vol24h, holders,
  age_min, mint_ca, canonical, first_deployed, endorsed_by, safety (jsonb), smart_money (jsonb)
narratives: id, title, blurb, meme_score, organic_score, combined_views, views_velocity,
  engagement_velocity, accel, gain_24h, age_min, lead_time_min, lifecycle, display_eligible,
  gate_reason, platforms, trend_term, search_series, top_post_id, img_seed, created_at
narrative_posts: media_url, image, text, posted_at (bigint, epoch MS -- use this for age)
API routes already wired: /api/holders, /api/safety, /api/toptraders (Birdeye,
  BIRDEYE_API_KEY provisioned), /api/trades, /api/token-lookup, /api/quote, /api/swap

STALE DOC: lib/types.ts:47 states "There is no mint address column on narrative_tickers."
That is no longer true -- worker/schema-token-lookup.sql:4 added `mint_ca`. Correct the
comment before an engineer designs around a constraint that was lifted.

--- DOES NOT EXIST. REQUIRED. ---

1. TABLE `coins` -- the missing entity. Keyed on mint (text PK), NOT on narrative_id.
   mint, symbol, name, logo_url, decimals
   creator_wallet            (from the PumpPortal create event we already consume)
   mint_time timestamptz     NOT age_min. See #2.
   launchpad                 'pumpfun' | 'bonk' | 'other' | 'unknown'
   curve_pct numeric         0-100, NULL once migrated
   migrated bool, migrated_at timestamptz, pool_address text
   band                      derived: 'fresh'|'graduating'|'live'
   socials jsonb             website / x / telegram
   first_seen_at, last_seen_at

2. `mint_time timestamptz` REPLACING `age_min`. age_min is a stored scalar -- it is wrong
   the second after it is written and there is no way to tell how wrong. Age is a render-time
   computation from a timestamp, always. Derive it as min(pairCreatedAt) across ALL Solana
   pairs for the mint, not from the best pair: comparePairs picks whichever pool later became
   most liquid, which for a mature token is an AMM pool created months post-mint (verified:
   418.3 days reported vs 646.8 days true for Fartcoin). For pre-graduation tokens the
   pumpfun pair IS the minimum, so one code path covers both regimes at zero extra network
   cost -- lookupMint() already holds data.pairs.

3. TABLE `coin_snapshots` -- there is NO price column anywhere in the schema and no time
   series for coins at all. post_snapshots exists for posts; the coin equivalent does not.
   Without it, every change window, every volume window and the entire ranking formula are
   uncomputable.
   mint, captured_at, price_usd, price_sol, mcap, liquidity,
   vol_buy_5m, vol_sell_5m, vol_buy_1h, vol_sell_1h, vol_24h,
   buys_5m, sells_5m, buyers_5m, sellers_5m, traders_5m, txns_24h,
   organic_buy_5m, organic_sell_5m, organic_score, organic_label,
   holder_count, top1_pct, top10_pct
   Retention: 5-minute grain for 48h, hourly rollup thereafter.

4. COLUMNS `price_usd`, `chg_5m`, `chg_1h`, `chg_24h`, `chg_since_mint`, `first_trade_price`
   -- materialised on `coins` from coin_snapshots, refreshed on the 20 s rank commit.
   chg_since_mint requires first_trade_price, which must be captured at the first observed
   trade or it is unrecoverable.

5. TABLE `coin_matches` -- match state has no home. `canonical` and `first_deployed` are
   booleans, not verdicts, and cannot express UNSURE.
   mint, narrative_id, match_state ('CONFIRMED'|'UNSURE'|'REJECTED'),
   relation ('DERIVED'|'ADOPTED'|'MENTIONED'|'SUGGESTED'),
   score numeric, calibrated bool,
   s_mint_in_post, s_img, s_text, s_tick, s_social,   <- the evidence vector, for the popover
   strong_channel_count int, time_prior numeric,
   lead_time_min int    (mint_time - narratives.promoted_at) -- the "+18m" chip
   matched_at, matcher_version
   UNIQUE(mint, narrative_id). Log EVERY confirmed and unsure row with its full vector --
   that is the eval set growing itself.

6. `narratives.promoted_at timestamptz` -- set ONCE, forever. The schema has created_at,
   first_seen_at and updated_at, none of which is the promote timestamp. lead_time_min
   exists as a column but has no defined origin without this. Every earliness claim on this
   board measures from promoted_at; if it can be rewritten, the honest record is fiction.

7. `narrative_tickers.source` -- 'cashtag' | 'llm' | 'mint_in_post'. Its absence is the root
   of the $KANG defect: extractTickers() keys LLM-invented tickers into the same Map as real
   cashtags with no provenance field, and an LLM ticker can become canonical. Do not delete
   suggested_ticker -- it is the earliest signal the product has -- separate it.

8. TABLE `creator_history` -- creator_wallet PK, prior_mints, median_peak_mcap, rug_count,
   best_peak_mcap, last_mint_at. Populated by a nightly job over the PumpPortal mint stream.
   Empty for ~14 days after launch; the row must render `?` during that period, never clean.

9. TABLE `coin_board_ticks` -- (band, captured_at, mint, rank, heat) for the 20 s rank commit,
   and p95_coinheat_1h per band for the presented-heat normalisation.

--- DELIBERATELY NOT MODELLED (render as `—`, never as green) ---
   dev_holding_pct, sniper_pct, bundle_pct, insider_pct. These need first-slot transaction
   analysis. A grey dash is honest; an absent chip reads as "fine."

--- QUERY SHAPES ---
Board (per band, served from a materialised view refreshed on the 20 s commit):
  SELECT c.mint, c.symbol, c.name, c.logo_url, c.mint_time, c.curve_pct, c.socials,
         c.price_usd, c.chg_5m, c.chg_1h, c.chg_24h, c.chg_since_mint,
         s.mcap, s.liquidity, s.vol_24h, s.vol_buy_5m + s.vol_sell_5m AS v5,
         s.holder_count, s.top10_pct, s.top1_pct, s.buys_5m, s.sells_5m,
         h.coin_heat, h.rank, h.unknown_signal_count,
         m.match_state, m.relation, m.lead_time_min,
         n.id AS narrative_id, n.title, n.img_seed, p.media_url
  FROM coin_board h
  JOIN coins c USING (mint)
  JOIN coin_snapshots_latest s USING (mint)
  LEFT JOIN coin_matches m ON m.mint = c.mint AND m.match_state IN ('CONFIRMED','UNSURE')
  LEFT JOIN narratives n ON n.id = m.narrative_id
  LEFT JOIN narrative_posts p ON p.id = n.top_post_id
  WHERE h.band = $1
  ORDER BY h.rank
  LIMIT 40;
One query, one round trip, no N+1 on the story cell. The LEFT JOIN returning NULL IS the
"no story" state -- it needs no separate branch.

Delta push: Supabase Broadcast on the board channel, payload = changed rows only, keyed by
mint. Positions apply on the tick; values apply immediately.

screens.name: Live Feed — Coins lane (the board)
screens.job: Rank what is moving right now inside a band where the comparison is meaningful, and tell the user where each coin came from before they click.
screens.layout:
Route /feed?lane=coins&band=fresh. Lane state and band state both in the URL — the current prototype has no URL at all (setView toggles a .on class, viewStack grows unbounded), and a trader cannot send a colleague a link to what they are looking at.

Shell is unchanged: 1fr content + 460px persistent right rail (aside.rail, §6.1), rail hidden <=1040px. Above the table: the lane tabs (see 'Toggle or two boards' below), then a band strip, then the table.

BAND STRIP — reuse .trend-subs / .trend-sub verbatim (§3, display:flex, gap:28px, Clash Display 16px/700, muted -> ink on .on, no underline, no pill). Four buttons: Fresh · Graduating · Live · From a Story. Each carries a mono 11px count in --dim after the label: 'Fresh 38'. 'From a Story' additionally gets a 6px cyan dot when its count changed in the last 60s — it is the only band a competitor cannot build and it should pull the eye.

BAND-SPECIFIC COLUMN SETS. This is the central layout decision. The Live band's column set is roughly 60% structurally empty on the Fresh band (no 1h, no 24h, no AMM liquidity, no 24h volume). Rendering four dashes per row across an entire band is not an edge case being handled, it is a table admitting it was designed for the wrong data. Each band gets its own header and grid template; one <CoinRow> component driven by a column config.

FRESH — 12 tracks:
  28px  minmax(196px,1.85fr)  minmax(140px,1.15fr)  56px  .62fr  .80fr  76px  .76fr  .60fr  .52fr  52px  72px
  #   ·  COIN  ·  STORY  ·  AGE  ·  PRICE  ·  MCAP  ·  CURVE  ·  VOL  ·  Δ MINT  ·  HLD  ·  RISK  ·  (action)

GRADUATING — same 12, CURVE promoted to position 4 (immediately after STORY) and is the sort key; Δ MINT swapped for LIQ. Progress is the question being asked in that band, so it sits where the eye lands after the identity columns.

LIVE — 14 tracks:
  28px  minmax(196px,1.85fr)  minmax(140px,1.15fr)  .62fr  .56fr .56fr .56fr  .76fr  .70fr  .80fr  .52fr  56px  52px  72px
  #  ·  COIN  ·  STORY  ·  PRICE  ·  5M  ·  1H  ·  24H  ·  VOL 24H  ·  LIQ  ·  MCAP  ·  HLD  ·  AGE  ·  RISK  ·  (action)

FROM A STORY — Live's set, but STORY widens to minmax(200px,1.6fr), COIN narrows to minmax(150px,1.2fr), and a LEAD column (56px, mono, lime) is inserted after STORY. In this band the story is the subject and the coin is the instrument; the columns should say so.

Row chrome: reuse .tk exactly — min-height 56px, padding 11px 16px, gap 10px, separator inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.035), hover background linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(61,224,255,.055), rgba(61,224,255,0) 42%) over #0C0C0E, and the .tk::before 2px cyan left accent bar at opacity 1 on hover with box-shadow 0 0 12px var(--ion).

RESPONSIVE — container queries on the table's own width, not the viewport, because the rail hiding at 1040px GIVES BACK 460px and a viewport media query gets the direction wrong. Drop order as width falls: HLD -> 24H -> LIQ -> VOL -> AGE. COIN, STORY, PRICE, MCAP, RISK and the action never drop. STORY surviving to the narrowest breakpoint is not negotiable — it is the differentiator; dropping it turns the board into DexScreener.

elements.shows: 1-40 in mono 11px --dim, centered. An unranked pre-rank row (see states) shows a dim '·' instead of a number.

elements.shows: 32px .tkico (border-radius 10px, logo overlay on SYMCOLOR fallback with first letter), symbol in General Sans 13.5px/600, name 10.5px --muted ellipsised beneath, then .socrow (14x14 .soc chips, 9x9 svg) in fixed order website / X / telegram / DexScreener / pump.fun. A NEW badge (.newbadge, mono 9px/700, #001318 on --lime) for the first 300s.
elements.source: coins.logo_url, coins.symbol, coins.name, coins.socials (all new)
elements.interaction: Row click -> coin page. Each .soc is an <a target=_blank> with stopPropagation.

elements.shows: Five states, never four. (1) CONFIRMED: 16px rounded story thumb + story title in General Sans 12px ellipsised + a lead chip 'origin +18m' in mono 10px lime on rgba(155,240,60,.10), meaning the story was display-eligible 18 minutes before this coin existed. A 1px cyan left hairline on the cell. (2) UNSURE: same layout, thumb at 60% opacity with a dashed 1px #2E2E36 ring, title in --muted, and the lead chip replaced by an amber 'UNVERIFIED' chip in mono 9px on rgba(255,184,77,.10). No cyan anywhere. (3) ADOPTED: story title with an amber 'ADOPTED' chip and the coin's TRUE age appended in --dim — the earliness claim is inverted here and concealing that is dishonest. (4) MATCHING: 'matching…' in --dim mono 10px with the existing .panel-loading pulse (opacity .55<->.95, 1.2s). (5) NONE: the literal string 'no story' in --dim mono 10px, uppercase, letter-spacing .06em, NO border, NO chip, NO box. Deliberately the quietest thing in the row — on the Fresh band this is 85-95% of rows and any badge treatment turns the column into noise.
elements.source: coin_matches.match_state / .relation / .lead_time_min (new table) LEFT JOIN narratives.title, narratives.img_seed, narrative_posts.media_url via narratives.top_post_id. lead_time_min = mint_time - narratives.promoted_at (promoted_at does not exist)
elements.interaction: CONFIRMED and ADOPTED: click -> story page, stopPropagation. UNSURE: click opens the evidence popover, NOT the story page — navigating on an unestablished claim asserts it; a second click inside the popover proceeds. Two steps, deliberately. NONE and MATCHING: not clickable, no cursor change.

elements.shows: '4m' / '2h' / '3d' in mono 11px. Under 60 minutes it renders in --ink rather than --muted; on a board selling earliness, age is a headline number, not chrome.
elements.source: now() - coins.mint_time, computed at render. NOT the stored age_min scalar, which is wrong the instant after it is written.
elements.interaction: Sortable. Default sort key on Fresh is heat, not age — 'newest' and 'hottest' are different questions and the band header says which one is active.

elements.shows: fmtP — $0.0000123 at 7dp below $0.01, else $1.2345. --ink, mono 12.5px, 600 weight. Flashes lime/red for 850ms on change via the existing .nm-tick-up / .nm-tick-down animation.
elements.source: coins.price_usd from coin_snapshots.price_usd (new). EXISTS for a 4-minute curve token — price is exact from the curve reserve ratio, and pump tokens are routable through Jupiter Price V3 from the first trade.
elements.interaction: Sortable.

elements.source: coin_snapshots.mcap. EXISTS at 4 minutes: pump.fun supply is a fixed 1,000,000,000, so mcap = price x 1e9 exactly. No vendor dependency.
elements.interaction: Sortable. Never a ranking term — see mechanism.

elements.shows: A 44px x 5px track (#131316, radius 3) with a fill (linear-gradient 90deg, var(--ion), #2E8CA6 — reuse the .hld-bar treatment), and the percentage in mono 10px right-aligned beneath. Above 80%, the fill switches to --lime and the number goes lime: that is the about-to-graduate state and it should be findable by peripheral vision alone.
elements.source: coins.curve_pct (new) = curve SOL reserve / graduation threshold. Threshold is SOL-denominated (~85 SOL); read it from the program, do not hardcode a USD number.
elements.interaction: Sortable — and it is the DEFAULT sort on the Graduating band. Renders as a 'DEX' badge (mono 9px, --dim, 1px --line border) on the Live band instead.

elements.shows: Fresh band header reads 'VOL 5M', but for a coin under 5 minutes old the cell shows volume since mint with the elapsed window as a mono 8px superscript ('$4.2K' over '3m'). Live band header reads 'VOL 24H'. The header text is band-dependent so the column's meaning is never ambiguous within a band.
elements.source: coin_snapshots.vol_buy_5m + vol_sell_5m, or .vol_24h (new)
elements.interaction: Sortable.

elements.shows: .chgpill — mono 11px, min-width 52px, padding 3px 7px, radius 6, tabular-nums, always signed to one decimal. .up lime on rgba(155,240,60,.10); .down red on rgba(255,92,110,.10). A cell whose window EXCEEDS the coin's age renders '—' in --dim with title='coin is 41m old' — never a 0.0% pill, which reads as 'flat' rather than 'undefined' and is the single most misleading render available here.
elements.source: coins.chg_5m / chg_1h / chg_24h from the coin_snapshots series (none exist)
elements.interaction: Sortable. The Fresh band never shows these columns at all — see Δ MINT.

elements.shows: The only change figure that is defined for a coin minutes old: percentage against the first observed trade price. Same .chgpill treatment. Replaces the 5M/1H/24H triplet rather than sitting alongside three dashes.
elements.source: (price_usd / coins.first_trade_price - 1). first_trade_price must be captured at the first observed trade or it is permanently unrecoverable — flag as new and as ORDER-DEPENDENT.
elements.interaction: Sortable. Default sort on Fresh after heat.

elements.shows: Integer, mono 11px. Under 25 holders it renders amber. THE BONDING CURVE PDA MUST BE EXCLUDED from the count and from the concentration math, or every pre-graduation token reads as 90% concentrated and the whole risk column collapses to red.
elements.source: /api/holders (Helius getTokenLargestAccounts — ALREADY WIRED) -> coin_snapshots.holder_count
elements.interaction: Sortable.

elements.shows: fmtUSD. On the Fresh/Graduating bands this figure is CURVE RESERVE, not an AMM pool — semantically a different quantity, and it is why LIQ is not shown on Fresh at all. It appears on Graduating (where reserve is the graduation fuel) and Live (where it is real pool depth).
elements.source: coin_snapshots.liquidity (new)
elements.interaction: Sortable.

elements.shows: 52px, mono 10px, centered. Shows the SINGLE WORST discriminating signal, never a composite score — a composite is a device for hiding which signal fired. Renders: 'T10 78' (red >60, amber 40-60) / 'H 11' amber for thin holders / 'NO SELL' red for the honeypot proxy / 'DEV x7' red for a creator with 7 prior mints and a sub-$15k median peak / a lime '✓' ONLY when at least 4 signals are known and all pass / '? 3' in --dim when 2 or more signals are unavailable. A clean tick can never be produced by absence of data — that is the entire design of this cell.
elements.source: coin_snapshots.top10_pct / top1_pct / holder_count / buys_5m / sells_5m (new), creator_history.* (new). dev_holding_pct, sniper_pct, bundle_pct are NOT MODELLED and contribute only to unknown_signal_count.
elements.interaction: Hover -> 260px popover listing all 8 signals; the four unobtainable ones are listed explicitly as 'not available at launch' rather than omitted, because a missing chip reads as 'fine'. Not sortable — sorting by a categorical worst-signal is meaningless.

elements.shows: 72px .buy — cyan #3DE0FF on #001318, radius 8, 12px/600. Label 'Buy'. NOT suppressed by an UNSURE story match: on this board the user selected the COIN, so the uncertainty is about provenance, not identity. D1's Buy-suppression applies on the STORY surface, where the question is 'buy which coin' — a naive implementation that suppresses here would grey out most of the board for a reason that does not apply. The uncertainty is carried entirely by the STORY cell.
elements.source: coins.mint -> Jupiter Swap V2 via /api/quote and /api/swap (already wired)
elements.interaction: Click -> coin page with the .tradebox focused; stopPropagation from the row. Wallet-disconnected still renders it live — see states.

states: DEFAULT — 40 rows, 20s rank commit, values updating every tick from a Map<mint,Row> while the ordering array is held. Freeze-on-hover queues reorders while the pointer is inside the table.

BRAND-NEW TOKEN, NO MARKET DATA — the defining state of this board. A coin seen on the mint stream with no trades yet has no V5, therefore no CoinHeat, therefore NO RANK. It renders in a pre-rank zone ABOVE row 1, max 5 rows, with '·' in the # column, values as '··' in --dim, a mono 'MINTED 8s AGO' chip counting up live, and a 1px dashed --line2 top border separating the zone from the ranked table. Unranked is not rank one, and rendering it as rank one would be the most consequential lie on the surface. Rows leave the zone on their first trade or after 90s.

MISSING WINDOW vs MISSING DATA — three visually distinct renders, because collapsing them is how a terminal misleads. (a) '—' in --dim = we cannot obtain this (dev%, bundle%). (b) '—' in --dim with a title attribute naming the coin's age = the window has not elapsed yet (24H on a 41-minute coin). (c) '··' in --dim = we expect this imminently and are waiting (a pre-first-trade price). Never 0, never 0.0%, never a green tick.

UNVERIFIED COIN MATCH — story cell in the UNSURE treatment: dashed ring, muted title, amber UNVERIFIED chip, no cyan, no lead chip. The row's Buy button is UNAFFECTED. The coin is excluded from the 'From a Story' band, which admits CONFIRMED only. Clicking the cell opens the evidence popover, not the story.

COIN WITH NO STORY — LEFT JOIN returns NULL; the cell renders 'no story' in --dim. No branch, no placeholder card, no 'find the story' CTA. This is the normal case, not a deficiency, and treating it as one would put a call to action on 90% of rows.

STALE PIPELINE — if the newest coin_snapshots.captured_at is more than 90s old, an amber banner mounts above the table: 'prices last updated 4m 12s ago — Jupiter feed degraded', with the age counting up live. Simultaneously every row's Buy button drops to the secondary outline treatment (.deploybtn skin: transparent, 1px cyan border) so no one-tap buy executes against a stale quote. Rows keep rendering with their last-known values — an empty board during a feed blip is the failure the incident log already contains.

SHOW RISKY OFF (default) — gated rows are absent and the band count reads '38 · 6 hidden'. The count of what is being withheld is always stated. The toggle is a visually loud switch in the band strip, not a checkbox in a drawer, because it relaxes a hard gate.

WALLET NOT CONNECTED — the Buy button renders fully live in its primary cyan treatment. Do NOT grey it out: the row action is navigation, and disabling the primary affordance on an unauthenticated board destroys the connect funnel. Click -> coin page -> .tradebox with the Privy modal raised and #quoteNote reading 'Connect wallet to trade'.

EMPTY BAND — .noresult, 44px padding, --muted. Per-band copy: 'No coins under 50% curve right now.' / 'Nothing approaching graduation.' / 'No story-linked coins in the last 6 hours — the matcher abstains when it is not sure.' The last one is the honest framing of an empty From-a-Story band and it doubles as an explanation of D1.

LOADING — 12 skeleton rows reusing the existing .ttr-skel treatment: .sk spans, linear-gradient(90deg, #131316, #1A1A1E 50%, #131316), background-size 200% 100%, animation skel 1.2s ease-in-out infinite. Skeleton widths match the band's column template so the layout does not jump.
NEW ENTRANTS ABOVE THE FOLD — batched into a cyan '3 new' pill pinned below the header; click applies. Rows never shove under the pointer.

ABSTAIN, BOARD-LEVEL — if the matcher's abstain rate exceeds 30% over the last hour, a dim mono line under the band strip reads 'matcher abstaining on 34% of candidates'. Per §5.7 a rising abstain rate is a signal about corpus staleness, not a failure — but it must be visible, not buried in an ops dashboard.

screens.name: Story evidence popover (from an UNSURE or CONFIRMED story cell)
screens.job: Show why the system believes this coin came from this story, using categorical language only, so the user can decide with the uncertainty visible.
screens.layout:
320px anchored popover, .sheet panel skin (linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,.02), transparent 120px) over #0C0C0E, 1px rgba(255,255,255,.055), radius 14, shadow 0 26px 64px -38px rgba(0,0,0,.85)). Three stacked regions: (1) side-by-side 88px squares — source post media left, token logo right, with a mono Δ between them reading 'minted 4m after the post'; (2) the evidence channel list; (3) the footer action.

This is the same surface §5.9 calls the earliness proof, so it is worth more design attention than its size suggests — it is where the product's central claim is either substantiated or exposed.

elements.shows: Source post image beside token logo, 88px each, with the temporal Δ rendered between them in mono 11px lime.
elements.source: narrative_posts.media_url via narratives.top_post_id; coins.logo_url; Δ = coins.mint_time - min(narrative_posts.posted_at)
elements.interaction: Static.

elements.shows: One line per channel that FIRED, in categorical words only, never numbers: 'name matches the story subject' / 'ticker matches, uncommon symbol' / 'the mint address appears in a tracked post' / 'logo matches the source image' / 'token metadata links the source post — unverified'. Channels that did not fire are omitted. NO percentage is rendered anywhere: per §5.9, a user shown '73% match' does their own thresholding and the abstain band stops functioning.
elements.source: coin_matches.s_mint_in_post / s_img / s_text / s_tick / s_social, thresholded server-side into strings (new table)
elements.interaction: Static.

elements.shows: CONFIRMED: 'matched' in lime. UNSURE: 'we are not confident this coin is related to this story' in amber, plain sentence, no hedging. ADOPTED: 'this coin existed before the story — the story attached to it' in amber, with the coin's true age.
elements.source: coin_matches.match_state, .relation
elements.interaction: Static.

elements.shows: CONFIRMED -> 'Open story →' in cyan. UNSURE -> 'View story anyway' in --muted outline treatment; the wording concedes the uncertainty rather than papering over it.
elements.source: narratives.id
elements.interaction: Navigates to the story page. From an UNSURE match the story page mounts with a persistent amber banner, and any Buy control there requires a second explicit confirm — never one-tap.

states: CONFIRMED — lime confidence line, cyan footer.
UNSURE — amber line, muted footer, two-step navigation.
ADOPTED — amber line, true coin age shown prominently, Δ region shows a NEGATIVE offset ('minted 173d before the post') rather than hiding it.

IMAGE CHANNEL NOT YET BUILT (phase 2) — the media pair still renders (it is the proof surface regardless) but no 'logo matches' line appears. The absence is silent; it is not claimed as a failed check.
STALE MATCH — matcher_version older than current: a dim mono footnote 'matched by an earlier version' rather than silently presenting an old verdict as current.

screens.name: Trending
screens.job: Answer the survey question 'what should I know about right now' across both stories and coins in one glance — a slower, higher-floor digest, not a second copy of the feed.
screens.layout:
Route /trending. NO TABS. Both mini-tables stacked in one scroll: 'Stories' (top 10) then 'Coins' (top 10), each with a .sr-section-hd (baseline space-between, title in Clash Display 15px/600, count in mono 11px --muted).

The reasoning: Trending is asked as one question, not two. Putting Narratives/Tokens sub-tabs here — as the current prototype does — forces two navigations to answer a single survey question, and hides half the answer behind a click. Tabs belong where the questions genuinely differ (the Live Feed); stacking belongs where the user wants a front page.

Reuse .trend-narr-mini and .trend-tok-mini verbatim (§3.1, §3.2), with two changes to the coins table: (a) the TOKEN cell gains a second line carrying the story title when a CONFIRMED match exists, in 10.5px --muted with a 10px cyan dot prefix — the story column, compressed to fit a 6-column mini-table; (b) a 40px RISK column before MCAP carrying the same worst-signal chip as the board.

Coins header becomes: # | TOKEN (+story line) | 24H | VOL | RISK | MCAP.

elements.shows: Unchanged from .trend-narr-mini: # | 42px thumb | title + 62-char snippet + platform marks | Views | Gain | Age | Mcap-or-Create.
elements.source: narratives.* — all exist
elements.interaction: Click -> story page. The Mcap cell falls back to the .btn-deploy-mini 'Create' pill when the story has zero confirmed coins, preserving the one rule.

elements.shows: 36px .tkico, symbol in 14px/600, name in 11px --muted, .socrow-mini beneath, and — new — a story line: a 10px cyan dot plus the story title in 10.5px --muted, ellipsised. Absent entirely when there is no confirmed match; no 'no story' text here, because at 10 rows the negative space reads correctly on its own and a repeated dim string would be visual static.
elements.source: coins.* (new) + coin_matches.match_state='CONFIRMED' + narratives.title
elements.interaction: Story line click -> story page, stopPropagation. Row click -> coin page.

elements.shows: Standard mono numerics. Trending's eligibility floor (age >= 30m) guarantees these windows are actually defined — which is precisely why Trending can use the 24h-weighted formula the Live Feed cannot.
elements.source: coins.chg_24h, coin_snapshots.vol_24h, .mcap (new)
elements.interaction: Not user-sortable — Trending is a curated view, and a sortable top-10 is just a bad version of the board.

elements.shows: Same worst-signal chip as the board, 40px.
elements.source: coin_snapshots + creator_history (new)
elements.interaction: Hover popover, identical to the board.

states: DEFAULT — 10 + 10, recomputed every 5 minutes. A mono 10px --dim line under each section header reads 'updated 2m ago'.

THIN MARKET — fewer than 10 coins clear the eligibility floor (mcap >= $30k, liq >= $5k, age >= 30m, vol24h >= $10k). Render only those that qualify and append a dim line: 'only 6 coins cleared the floor in the last 24h.' Never backfill with junk to reach ten — a padded top-10 is the same lie as a hits-only track record.
NO STORY-LINKED COINS IN THE TOP 10 — no special treatment. The absence is the honest signal, and manufacturing a story-linked row to prove the thesis would corrupt the thing being proved.

STALE PIPELINE — the amber banner from the board applies to the Coins section only; the Stories section is fed by a different pipeline and must be able to fail independently. Two feeds, two failure states, stated separately.
LOADING — .narr-loading / .noresult copy, 'Loading…' in --muted 13px, count chip shows '…'.
SAMPLE DATA — the existing .narr-data-tag (mono 10px, #ffb020, 1px rgba(255,176,32,.35), 'using sample data') mounts beside the section title whenever the surface is not on live data.

buildOrder: 1. SCHEMA — the `coins` table keyed on mint, not narrative_id. Backfill from narrative_tickers.mint_ca. Nothing else on this list is possible first, because the coin lane currently has no entity: narrative_tickers cannot store a coin that has no story, and that is 85-95% of every row on this board.

2. `mint_time timestamptz` derived as min(pairCreatedAt) across ALL Solana pairs for the mint (lookupMint() already holds data.pairs — zero extra network cost). Delete `if (!pair.pairCreatedAt) return 0;` at lib/token-lookup.js:70 and fail closed instead. Retire the age_min scalar. Ship as its own step: it is a correctness fix that stands alone and it corrects a live 228-day error on mature tokens plus a 'brand new' misrender on missing data.

3. `coin_snapshots` on the Jupiter Tokens V2 Developer tier ($25/mo, 10 RPS — the free 1 RPS is shared across Swap, Price and Token calls, so one user working the trade panel would starve the board). 5-minute grain, 48h retention. This unlocks price, every change window, every volume window and the entire ranking formula in one step.

4. The board with the Fresh band ONLY, ranked by CoinHeat_fresh with quality_cold. No story column yet, no risk chip. This is a shippable terminal on its own and it validates the ranking before any of the harder columns exist.

5. Risk chip + safety multiplier from the signals already wired: /api/holders and /api/safety exist today. Excluding the bonding-curve PDA from concentration math is part of this step, not a follow-up — without it the column is uniformly red and worthless.
6. The remaining three bands. Graduating needs coins.curve_pct; Live needs the AMM pool join. From a Story is deferred to step 8 because it depends on the matcher.

7. `coin_matches` + `narratives.promoted_at` + `narrative_tickers.source`. Ship the §5.10 Day-1 matcher fixes together here: stop feeding suggested_ticker into enrichment, majors blocklist on the DERIVED path, the G2 temporal veto, a hard exact-symbol filter in pickBestPair, liquidity filter BEFORE ranking rather than rejection after, collision IDF, and the >=2-strong-channel rule. Scope this honestly at 40+ lines across three files plus a migration and a backfill, not the five-line change it has been described as.
8. The STORY column with all five states, and the 'From a Story' band. This is the step that makes the product differentiated; everything before it is a competent clone of DexScreener.

9. Trending — reuse .trend-narr-mini and .trend-tok-mini, add the story line and the risk column, apply the eligibility floor. Cheap once steps 3-8 land, and deliberately last: a digest of data that is not yet trustworthy is worse than no digest.

10. `creator_history` from the PumpPortal mint stream already running as the earliness clock. Ships dark, accumulates for ~14 days, then the DEV signal turns on in the risk chip. Until it has data the chip must show '?', never a tick.

11. Realtime — Supabase Broadcast on the board channel, plus the five rank-stability mechanisms (EPS_SWAP .08, ENTER 2, EXIT 3, PIN 90s, MAX_MOVE 5), freeze-on-hover, and the batched new-entrant pill. Last, because it is a polish layer over a board that must already be correct.
openQuestions: THE GRADUATION THRESHOLD IS SOL-DENOMINATED (~85 SOL) AND MOVES WITH SOL PRICE. curve_pct must be computed from the SOL reserve against the program's own constant, not from a $69k USD figure. Confirm the current constant from the deployed program and re-read it rather than pinning it — and decide whether the same lane logic should apply to Bonk/other launchpads with different thresholds, or whether they get their own band.

THE BONDING-CURVE PDA'S SHARE OF SUPPLY: I have specified excluding it from concentration and holder counts. Confirm empirically against 20 live pre-graduation tokens that Helius getTokenLargestAccounts returns the curve account in a form that is reliably identifiable, and that excluding it yields a top10_pct distribution with real spread rather than one clustered near 100%. If it does not discriminate even after exclusion, the risk chip on the Fresh band collapses to holders + honeypot + creator, and that should be known before the column is designed around it.

IS 40 ROWS PER BAND RIGHT, OR SHOULD FRESH BE DEEPER? Fresh turns over in ~40 minutes and a trader hunting the earliest entry may want 100 rows. Deeper costs nothing server-side (one materialised view) but dilutes the 'ranked' claim. Founder call.

THE 'FROM A STORY' BAND WILL BE THIN AT LAUNCH — plausibly 3-8 rows. Recall@CONFIRMED is targeted at 0.55-0.70 and the abstain band is 15-30% by design, so the band that best demonstrates the thesis is also the emptiest. Is a 5-row band shipped as-is, or does it stay behind a flag until the matcher has volume? Shipping it thin is more honest and consistent with D2; hiding it is more flattering. This is a D2-adjacent judgement call and it should be made deliberately, not by default.

chg_since_mint REQUIRES first_trade_price CAPTURED AT THE FIRST OBSERVED TRADE. If the coin is discovered late, that value is permanently unrecoverable and the Fresh band's only defined change column is empty for that row. Decide the fallback: earliest observed price with a 'from first seen' qualifier, or an honest dash. I lean toward the qualifier, because a dash on the Fresh band's only change column reads as broken.

JUPITER'S ORGANIC CLASSIFICATION FAILS FALSE-POSITIVE BY CONSTRUCTION — a wallet is flagged non-organic only on identifiable sniper/copy-trade patterns, and everything else defaults to organic. For a product where a false positive means the user buys a rug, is org allowed in the quality term at all before the Helius holder-distribution cross-check is running, or does quality_cold apply universally until then? Safest reading is quality_cold everywhere at launch.

SHOULD THE BOARD EVER SHOW PRESENTED HEAT AS A NUMBER? Stories show heat 0-100. Doing the same for coins gives users a sortable column, but §5.9's argument against rendering '73% match' beside an actionable control arguably extends to rendering '84 heat' beside a Buy button. My inclination is heat drives the ordering and is never rendered on the coins lane — rank position IS the display of heat — but this contradicts nothing explicitly and should be confirmed.

AT WHAT LATENCY DOES THE STALE BANNER FIRE? I have specified 90s. That is a guess calibrated to a 20s rank commit; it needs a measurement of the real p95 gap on the Jupiter Developer tier at 10 RPS across ~40 tracked mints before it is fixed, or the banner will either cry wolf or never appear.
